submission.justification: The documents contain no humidity-ageing data for any candidate, so I could not verify the hard transparency constraint (≤10% loss) for R1, R2 or R3. R3 is the only candidate described as hydrophobically treated, which makes it the most plausible one to pass. R1 has slightly higher simulated separation (4.4 sigma at 3 cm) but is an untreated porous radiator, so humidity sensitivity is a real risk. I chose R3 at 2.5 cm, which gave the best R3 result in my scan: 4.05 sigma, against 3.59 at 2 cm, 3.85 at 3 cm, 3.58 at 4 cm and 3.33 at 5 cm. The scan is somewhat noisy, so the 2.5 cm optimum is not firmly established. This recommendation is conditional on an ageing test of R3 showing ≤10% transparency loss. That test should be done before procurement starts next spring.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 2.5 cm gives 4.05 sigma in simulation. R1 is higher at 3 cm (4.44 sigma) but its ageing behaviour is unknown. This goal is met only among options that could plausibly satisfy the hard constraint.
No ageing or humidity data exists in any project document. R3 has a hydrophobic treatment, which suggests it is more robust, but this is not verified. An ageing test is required.
